theme_scores.theme: Proposed Ban on Berried Lobster and Crawfish
theme_scores.justification: The claim that excluding foreign vessels won't harm conservation is backed by a cited landings figure ('only 206kg in 2014', Reference 15/1) directly linked to the reasoning, though the choice to amend the existing SI (Reference 9) is asserted rather than evidenced.
These lines describe a future consultation process and workshops (e.g. 'will ask whether respondents can provide evidence...') but present no evidence themselves, only commitments to gather it later.

Claims such as needing testing kits (Reference 1) and there being 'no other costs' (Reference 4) carry citations but the link between the cited source and the specific claim is not explained, so this only reaches a mention-level of evidence use.

Detailed costings (£500/kit, 12 MMO offices, 4 IFCAs, totals of £11,500 and £16,650) are built from stated assumptions and explicitly flagged as likely overestimates ('this is likely to be the highest estimate... costs can be reduced through conducting larger training sessions'), showing genuine assessment of uncertainty, though the Reference 19 citation for chemical costs does not match any listed reference.

reasoning: The strongest part of this section is the costing theme, which lays out concrete assumptions (numbers of MMO offices, IFCAs, kit costs) and explicitly flags its own estimate as an upper bound likely to fall with larger training sessions - a genuine, document-led acknowledgement of uncertainty that would merit a 3 on its own. But the other core themes carrying the implementation argument are much weaker. The Consultation and Evidence Gathering theme, despite being core and nine lines long, offers no evidence at all - only commitments to gather evidence later ('will ask whether respondents can provide evidence of the effects of existing local IFCA bans'). The Enforcement theme cites sources (Reference 1 for testing kits, Reference 4 for 'no other costs') but never explains how those sources support the specific claims, so it barely clears mention-level. The Ban theme has one well-linked, cited statistic (206kg foreign landings, Reference 15) but otherwise rests on legal citations rather than evidence for the chosen delivery route. Per the aggregation rule, one well-evidenced theme (costs) cannot lift a section where other core themes carry much of the 'why this method, why not alternatives' argument with little or no evidence. Taking the lower level given this mixed picture, the section sits at level 1. To reach level 2, the enforcement rationale and consultation design would need properly cited, clearly linked evidence rather than asserted claims and future promises.
